name: Distance-based Gaussian Splatting
definition: An approach that builds a connection between a large-scale mesh and Gaussian splats by classifying splats as tightly-bound or loosely-bound based on their distance to the mesh surface, and masking out splats occluded by the mesh.
summary: Distance-based Gaussian Splatting constructs high-fidelity radiance fields by classifying splats as tightly or loosely bound to a mesh, reducing redundancy and artifacts through adaptive alignment and occlusion culling.
